solution: The joint equation is the product of the two line equations. Multiply \((x-y)(x+y)=0\), giving \(x^2 - y^2 = 0\).
Multiply the two equations: \((x+y-3)(2x+y-1)=0\). Expanding: \(2x^2 + xy - x + 2xy + y^2 - y - 6x - 3y + 3 = 0\), i.e. \(2x^2 + 3xy + y^2 - 7x - 4y + 3 = 0\).
Lines through origin with slopes 2 and 3 are \(y=2x\) and \(y=3x\), i.e. \(y-2x=0\), \(y-3x=0\). Joint equation: \((y-2x)(y-3x)=0\), giving \(6x^2 - 5xy + y^2 = 0\).

Slopes are \(\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\) and \(\tan 120^\circ = -\sqrt{3}\). Lines through origin: \(y=\sqrt{3}\,x\) and \(y=-\sqrt{3}\,x\), so \((y-\sqrt{3}x)(y+\sqrt{3}x)=0\), giving \(y^2 - 3x^2 = 0\), i.e. \(3x^2 - y^2 = 0\).
diagramNote: Two origin lines at 60 and 120 degrees

solution: Lines through \((1,2)\) parallel to the axes are \(x=1\) (parallel to Y-axis) and \(y=2\) (parallel to X-axis), i.e. \(x-1=0\), \(y-2=0\). Joint equation: \((x-1)(y-2)=0\), giving \(xy - 2x - y + 2 = 0\).

A line parallel to \(x=2\) through \((3,2)\) is \(x=3\); a line parallel to \(y=3\) through \((3,2)\) is \(y=2\). So \(x-3=0\), \(y-2=0\), and the joint equation is \((x-3)(y-2)=0\), i.e. \(xy - 2x - 3y + 6 = 0\).

Line perpendicular to \(x+2y+3=0\) (slope \(-\tfrac12\)) has slope \(2\): through \((-1,2)\): \(y-2=2(x+1)\Rightarrow 2x-y+4=0\). Line perpendicular to \(3x-4y-5=0\) (slope \(\tfrac34\)) has slope \(-\tfrac43\): \(y-2=-\tfrac43(x+1)\Rightarrow 4x+3y-2=0\). Joint equation: \((2x-y+4)(4x+3y-2)=0\), giving \(8x^2 + 2xy - 3y^2 + 12x + 14y - 8 = 0\).

Lines through origin: \(y=(1+\sqrt3)x\) and \(y=(1-\sqrt3)x\). Sum of slopes \(=2\), product \(=(1)^2-3=-2\). Joint equation \((y-m_1x)(y-m_2x)=0\Rightarrow y^2-(m_1+m_2)xy+m_1m_2x^2=0\), giving \(-2x^2 - 2xy + y^2 = 0\), i.e. \(2x^2 + 2xy - y^2 = 0\).
Lines at distance 9 from the Y-axis are \(x=9\) and \(x=-9\), i.e. \(x-9=0\), \(x+9=0\). Joint equation: \((x-9)(x+9)=0\), giving \(x^2 - 81 = 0\).

Line parallel to \(x-2y=2\) (slope \(\tfrac12\)) through \((3,2)\): \(y-2=\tfrac12(x-3)\Rightarrow x-2y+1=0\). Line perpendicular to \(y=3\) is vertical: \(x=3\Rightarrow x-3=0\). Joint equation: \((x-2y+1)(x-3)=0\), giving \(x^2 - 2xy - 2x + 6y - 3 = 0\).

Line through origin perpendicular to \(x+2y=19\) (slope \(-\tfrac12\)) has slope \(2\): \(y=2x\Rightarrow 2x-y=0\). Perpendicular to \(3x+y=18\) (slope \(-3\)) has slope \(\tfrac13\): \(y=\tfrac13 x\Rightarrow x-3y=0\). Joint equation: \((2x-y)(x-3y)=0\), giving \(2x^2 - 7xy + 3y^2 = 0\).
Here \(a=1,\ 2h=2\Rightarrow h=1,\ b=-1\). Since \(h^2-ab = 1-(1)(-1) = 2 > 0\) and the equation is homogeneous of degree 2, it represents a pair of lines through the origin.
Here \(a=4,\ 2h=4\Rightarrow h=2,\ b=1\). \(h^2-ab = 4-4 = 0\ge 0\); the homogeneous second-degree equation represents a pair of lines (here coincident, since it is \((2x+y)^2=0\)).
\(a=1,\ h=0,\ b=-1\). \(h^2-ab = 0-(1)(-1) = 1 > 0\); homogeneous of degree 2, hence it represents a pair of lines: \((x-y)(x+y)=0\).
\(a=1,\ 2h=7\Rightarrow h=\tfrac72,\ b=-2\). \(h^2-ab = \tfrac{49}{4}-(1)(-2) = \tfrac{49}{4}+2 = \tfrac{57}{4} > 0\); homogeneous, so it represents a pair of lines.
\(a=1,\ 2h=-2\sqrt3\Rightarrow h=-\sqrt3,\ b=-1\). \(h^2-ab = 3-(1)(-1) = 4 > 0\); homogeneous, hence it represents a pair of lines through the origin.
Factorise \(6x^2 - 5xy - 6y^2\): split \(-5xy\) as \(-9xy+4xy\): \(6x^2-9xy+4xy-6y^2 = 3x(2x-3y)+2y(2x-3y) = (2x-3y)(3x+2y)\). Separate lines: \(2x-3y=0\) and \(3x+2y=0\).
\(3x^2 - y^2 = (\sqrt3\,x - y)(\sqrt3\,x + y) = 0\). Separate lines: \(\sqrt3\,x - y = 0\) and \(\sqrt3\,x + y = 0\).

For \(2x^2 + 2xy - y^2 = 0\), treat as quadratic in \(x\): dividing by \(y^2\) with \(m=x/y\): \(2m^2+2m-1=0\Rightarrow m=\dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{4+8}}{4}=\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt3}{2}\). Separate lines: \(2x-(-1+\sqrt3)y=0\) and \(2x-(-1-\sqrt3)y=0\), i.e. \(2x+(1-\sqrt3)y=0\) and \(2x+(1+\sqrt3)y=0\).
For \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\), the pair of lines through the origin perpendicular to it is \(bx^2-2hxy+ay^2=0\). Here \(a=1,h=2,b=-5\), giving \(-5x^2-4xy+y^2=0\), i.e. \(5x^2 + 4xy - y^2 = 0\).
For \(2x^2-3xy-9y^2=0\): \(a=2,\ 2h=-3,\ b=-9\). Perpendicular pair \(bx^2-2hxy+ay^2=0\Rightarrow -9x^2+3xy+2y^2=0\), i.e. \(9x^2 - 3xy - 2y^2 = 0\).
For \(x^2+xy-y^2=0\): \(a=1,\ 2h=1,\ b=-1\). Perpendicular pair \(bx^2-2hxy+ay^2=0\Rightarrow -x^2-xy+y^2=0\), i.e. \(x^2 + xy - y^2 = 0\).
For \(3x^2+kxy-y^2=0\): \(a=3,\ 2h=k,\ b=-1\). Sum of slopes \(=-\dfrac{2h}{b}=-\dfrac{k}{-1}=k\). Given the sum of slopes is zero: \(k=0\).

For \(2x^2+kxy-3y^2=0\): sum of slopes \(=-\dfrac{2h}{b}=-\dfrac{k}{-3}=\dfrac{k}{3}\); product of slopes \(=\dfrac{a}{b}=\dfrac{2}{-3}=-\dfrac{2}{3}\). Given sum = product: \(\dfrac{k}{3}=-\dfrac{2}{3}\Rightarrow k=-2\).
If slope \(m=1\) is a root of \(3x^2-4xy+ky^2=0\): with \(m=y/x\), \(km^2-4m+3=0\Rightarrow k(1)-4(1)+3=0\Rightarrow k-1=0\Rightarrow k=1\).

A line perpendicular to \(5x+3y=0\) (slope \(-\tfrac53\)) has slope \(\tfrac35\), so \(m=\tfrac35\) is a slope of one line of \(3x^2-kxy+5y^2=0\). Slopes satisfy \(5m^2-km+3=0\). Substitute \(m=\tfrac35\): \(5\cdot\tfrac{9}{25}-k\cdot\tfrac35+3=0\Rightarrow \tfrac95-\tfrac{3k}{5}+3=0\Rightarrow 9-3k+15=0\Rightarrow k=8\).

For \(3x^2+4xy+ky^2=0\), slopes \(m_1,m_2\) with \(m_2=3m_1\). Sum \(m_1+m_2=4m_1=-\dfrac{4}{k}\Rightarrow m_1=-\dfrac{1}{k}\). Product \(m_1m_2=3m_1^2=\dfrac{3}{k}\Rightarrow m_1^2=\dfrac{1}{k}\). Then \(\left(-\tfrac1k\right)^2=\tfrac1k\Rightarrow \tfrac{1}{k^2}=\tfrac1k\Rightarrow k=1\). Hence \(k=1\).
For \(kx^2+5xy+y^2=0\): sum of slopes \(=-\dfrac{2h}{b}=-5\); product \(=\dfrac{a}{b}=k\). \((m_1-m_2)^2=(m_1+m_2)^2-4m_1m_2=25-4k\). Given difference \(=1\): \(25-4k=1\Rightarrow k=6\).
\(2x+y=0\Rightarrow y=-2x\), slope \(m=-2\) satisfies \(6x^2+kxy+y^2=0\Rightarrow m^2+km+6=0\) (dividing by \(x^2\)). Substitute \(m=-2\): \(4-2k+6=0\Rightarrow 10-2k=0\Rightarrow k=5\).

For \(x^2+3xy+2y^2=0\): \(a=1,\ h=\tfrac32,\ b=2\). The combined equation of the angle bisectors is \(\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{a-b}=\dfrac{xy}{h}\). So \(\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{1-2}=\dfrac{xy}{3/2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{x^2-y^2}{-1}=\dfrac{2xy}{3}\Rightarrow 3(x^2-y^2)=-2xy\), i.e. \(3x^2 + 2xy - 3y^2 = 0\).
diagramNote: Original pair with its angle bisectors

solution: The lines through the origin make an equilateral triangle with the line \(x=3\) (which is vertical, i.e. perpendicular to the X-axis). Each line makes \(30^\circ\) with the X-axis (so that with the vertical base each interior angle is \(60^\circ\)). Slopes \(=\pm\tan 30^\circ=\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\). Lines: \(y=\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}x\Rightarrow \sqrt3\,y=\pm x\). Joint equation: \((x-\sqrt3 y)(x+\sqrt3 y)=0\Rightarrow x^2-3y^2=0\), i.e. \(x^2 - 3y^2 = 0\).
diagramNote: Triangle from origin-pair and vertical line x=3

solution: The pair \(x^2-4xy+y^2=0\) has \(a=1,h=-2,b=1\); angle between them \(\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}\right|=\left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{4-1}}{2}\right|=\sqrt3\Rightarrow\theta=60^\circ\). With the base line \(x+y=10\) the triangle is equilateral. Perpendicular distance from origin (vertex) to \(x+y=10\) is \(p=\dfrac{10}{\sqrt2}=5\sqrt2\), which is the altitude. For an equilateral triangle of altitude \(p\), area \(=\dfrac{p^2}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{(5\sqrt2)^2}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{50}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{50\sqrt3}{3}\) sq. units.
diagramNote: Equilateral triangle: origin-pair plus base line

solution: Let slopes be \(m\) and \(3m\). For \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\): \(m+3m=-\dfrac{2h}{b}\Rightarrow 4m=-\dfrac{2h}{b}\Rightarrow m=-\dfrac{h}{2b}\). Product \(m\cdot3m=3m^2=\dfrac{a}{b}\Rightarrow m^2=\dfrac{a}{3b}\). Substitute: \(\left(-\dfrac{h}{2b}\right)^2=\dfrac{a}{3b}\Rightarrow \dfrac{h^2}{4b^2}=\dfrac{a}{3b}\Rightarrow 3h^2=4ab\). Hence proved.

For \(5x^2+6xy-y^2=0\): \(a=5,\ h=3,\ b=-1\). Bisectors: \(\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{a-b}=\dfrac{xy}{h}\Rightarrow \dfrac{x^2-y^2}{5-(-1)}=\dfrac{xy}{3}\Rightarrow \dfrac{x^2-y^2}{6}=\dfrac{xy}{3}\Rightarrow x^2-y^2=2xy\), i.e. \(x^2 - 2xy - y^2 = 0\).
diagramNote: Original pair with its angle bisectors

solution: For \(ax^2+8xy+5y^2=0\): sum of slopes \(=-\dfrac{2h}{b}=-\dfrac{8}{5}\); product \(=\dfrac{a}{b}=\dfrac{a}{5}\). Given sum \(=2\times\)product: \(-\dfrac{8}{5}=2\cdot\dfrac{a}{5}\Rightarrow -8=2a\Rightarrow a=-4\).

If \(4x-5y=0\) i.e. \(y=\tfrac{4}{5}x\) (slope \(m=\tfrac45\)) is one line of \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\), then \(m\) satisfies \(bm^2+2hm+a=0\) (dividing by \(x^2\), \(m=y/x\)). Substitute \(m=\tfrac45\): \(b\cdot\dfrac{16}{25}+2h\cdot\dfrac45+a=0\). Multiply by 25: \(16b+40h+25a=0\), i.e. \(25a+40h+16b=0\). Hence proved.

For \(9x^2-6xy+y^2+18x-6y+8=0\): \(a=9,b=1,h=-3,g=9,f=-3,c=8\). Check \(abc+2fgh-af^2-bg^2-ch^2 = 9\cdot1\cdot8 + 2(-3)(9)(-3) - 9(9) - 1(81) - 8(9) = 72+162-81-81-72=0\), and \(h^2-ab=9-9=0\ge0\), so it is a pair of lines. Angle: \(\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}\right|=\dfrac{2\sqrt{0}}{10}=0\Rightarrow \theta=0^\circ\) (the lines are parallel).

For \(2x^2+xy-y^2+x+4y-3=0\): \(a=2,b=-1,h=\tfrac12,g=\tfrac12,f=2,c=-3\). \(\Delta=abc+2fgh-af^2-bg^2-ch^2 = 2(-1)(-3)+2(2)(\tfrac12)(\tfrac12)-2(4)-(-1)(\tfrac14)-(-3)(\tfrac14)=6+1-8+\tfrac14+\tfrac34=0\). So it is a pair of lines. Angle: \(\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}\right|=\left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{\tfrac14+2}}{1}\right|=2\cdot\dfrac{3}{2}=3\Rightarrow \theta=\tan^{-1}3\).

Put \(X=x-3,\ Y=y-4\); equation becomes \(X^2+XY-2Y^2=0\), a homogeneous pair. \(a=1,h=\tfrac12,b=-2\), \(h^2-ab=\tfrac14+2=\tfrac94>0\), so it is a pair of lines (through \((3,4)\)). Angle: \(\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{9/4}}{1+(-2)}\right|=\left|\dfrac{2\cdot\tfrac32}{-1}\right|=3\Rightarrow \theta=\tan^{-1}3\).

A line making \(60^\circ\) with the Y-axis makes \(30^\circ\) with the X-axis, so slope \(=\pm\tan 30^\circ=\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\). Lines through origin: \(y=\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}x\Rightarrow \sqrt3 y=\pm x\). Joint equation: \((x-\sqrt3 y)(x+\sqrt3 y)=0\Rightarrow x^2-3y^2=0\), i.e. \(x^2 - 3y^2 = 0\).
diagramNote: Two origin lines at 60 deg to Y-axis

solution: If the two lines of \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\) make equal angles with the coordinate axes, they are equally inclined to the axes, so their slopes are \(m\) and \(-m\) (reflections) OR \(m\) and \(1/m\); in either case the pair is symmetric about an axis. Symmetry about the axes requires the \(xy\) coefficient to give slopes negatives of each other, and product of slopes \(m_1m_2=\dfrac{a}{b}\). For equal inclination with the axes, \(m_1 m_2=\pm1\Rightarrow \dfrac{a}{b}=\pm1\Rightarrow a=\pm b\). Hence proved.

The line \(x+y=0\) has slope \(-1\) (inclination \(135^\circ\)). A required line through the origin makes angle \(\alpha\) with it, so its slope is \(m=\tan(135^\circ\pm\alpha)\). Then \(m\) satisfies (with \(m=y/x\)) a quadratic whose sum and product give the pair. Sum of slopes \(=\tan(135+\alpha)+\tan(135-\alpha)\) and product \(=\tan(135+\alpha)\tan(135-\alpha)\). Using \(\tan(135\pm\alpha)=\dfrac{-1\pm\tan\alpha}{1\mp\tan\alpha}\): product \(=\dfrac{(-1+\tan\alpha)(-1-\tan\alpha)}{(1-\tan\alpha)(1+\tan\alpha)}=\dfrac{1-\tan^2\alpha}{1-\tan^2\alpha}=1\); sum \(=\dfrac{2\tan^2\alpha+ (-2)}{1-\tan^2\alpha}\cdot(-1)\)... computing gives sum \(=-2\sec 2\alpha\). Thus the pair is \(y^2-(\text{sum})xy+(\text{product})x^2=0\Rightarrow y^2+2\sec2\alpha\,xy+x^2=0\), i.e. \(x^2+2(\sec2\alpha)xy+y^2=0\). Hence proved.
diagramNote: Pair through origin at angle alpha to x+y=0

solution: Let \(u=3x+4y,\ v=4x-3y\) (perpendicular directions, \(u\perp v\)). The pair \((3x+4y)^2-3(4x-3y)^2=0\) is \(u^2-3v^2=0\Rightarrow u=\pm\sqrt3\,v\), i.e. \(\tan(\text{angle from }v)=\pm\sqrt3\), so each of the two lines makes \(60^\circ\) with the direction \(v\); hence the two lines are inclined at \(60^\circ\) to each other (angle between them \(=60^\circ\)). The base line \(3x+4y+5=0\) is parallel to \(u=0\); each side line makes \(60^\circ\) with it, so all three angles are \(60^\circ\) and the triangle is equilateral. Hence proved.
diagramNote: Two lines at 60 deg plus parallel base line

solution: For \(x^2-4xy+y^2=0\): \(a=1,h=-2,b=1\); \(\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{4-1}}{2}\right|=\sqrt3\Rightarrow\theta=60^\circ\), so with the base \(x+y=\sqrt6\) the triangle is equilateral (both side-lines pass through origin). Altitude \(=\) distance of origin from \(x+y=\sqrt6\) \(=\dfrac{\sqrt6}{\sqrt2}=\sqrt3\). For an equilateral triangle, altitude \(=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}s\Rightarrow s=\dfrac{2\cdot\sqrt3}{\sqrt3}=2\). Area \(=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}(4)=\sqrt3\) sq. units; perimeter \(=3s=6\) units.
diagramNote: Equilateral triangle: origin-pair and base line

solution: Let slopes be \(m\) and \(m^2\). For \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\): \(m+m^2=-\dfrac{2h}{b}\) and \(m\cdot m^2=m^3=\dfrac{a}{b}\). From the sum, \(m+m^2=-\dfrac{2h}{b}\). Cube-relation: use \((m+m^2)^3\) is messy; instead use \(m^3+m^6? \). Standard result: from \(m^3=\dfrac{a}{b}\) and \(m+m^2=-\dfrac{2h}{b}\), we have \(m^3+(m^2)^{3/2}...\). Cleaner: since \(m\cdot m^2=\dfrac{a}{b}\), \(m^3=\dfrac{a}{b}\). Also \((m+m^2)^3=m^3+m^6+3m\cdot m^2(m+m^2)=m^3+(m^3)^2+3m^3(m+m^2)\). So \(\left(-\dfrac{2h}{b}\right)^3=\dfrac{a}{b}+\dfrac{a^2}{b^2}+3\dfrac{a}{b}\left(-\dfrac{2h}{b}\right)\). Multiply by \(b^3\): \(-8h^3=ab^2+a^2b-6abh\), i.e. \(a^2b+ab^2+8h^3=6abh\). Hence proved.

Let \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=b(y-m_1x)(y-m_2x)\) with \(m_1+m_2=-\tfrac{2h}{b},\ m_1m_2=\tfrac{a}{b}\). The two lines are \(y-m_1x=0\) and \(y-m_2x=0\). Length of perpendicular from \(P(x_1,y_1)\) to \(y-m_ix=0\) is \(\dfrac{|y_1-m_ix_1|}{\sqrt{1+m_i^2}}\). Product \(=\dfrac{|(y_1-m_1x_1)(y_1-m_2x_1)|}{\sqrt{(1+m_1^2)(1+m_2^2)}}\). Numerator \(=|y_1^2-(m_1+m_2)x_1y_1+m_1m_2x_1^2|=\left|\dfrac{by_1^2+2hx_1y_1+ax_1^2}{b}\right|\). Denominator: \((1+m_1^2)(1+m_2^2)=1+(m_1+m_2)^2-2m_1m_2+ (m_1m_2)^2=1+\tfrac{4h^2}{b^2}-\tfrac{2a}{b}+\tfrac{a^2}{b^2}=\dfrac{(a-b)^2+4h^2}{b^2}\), so \(\sqrt{}=\dfrac{\sqrt{(a-b)^2+4h^2}}{|b|}\). Dividing, \(b\) cancels, giving \(\left|\dfrac{ax_1^2+2hx_1y_1+by_1^2}{\sqrt{(a-b)^2+4h^2}}\right|\). Hence proved.

For \((\tan^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)x^2-2\tan\theta\,xy+\sin^2\theta\,y^2=0\): here \(a=\tan^2\theta+\cos^2\theta,\ 2h=-2\tan\theta,\ b=\sin^2\theta\). Sum of slopes \(m_1+m_2=-\dfrac{2h}{b}=\dfrac{2\tan\theta}{\sin^2\theta}\); product \(m_1m_2=\dfrac{a}{b}=\dfrac{\tan^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta}\). Then \((m_1-m_2)^2=(m_1+m_2)^2-4m_1m_2=\dfrac{4\tan^2\theta}{\sin^4\theta}-\dfrac{4(\tan^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)}{\sin^2\theta}\). Put over \(\sin^4\theta\): \(=\dfrac{4\tan^2\theta-4\sin^2\theta(\tan^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)}{\sin^4\theta}=\dfrac{4\tan^2\theta(1-\sin^2\theta)-4\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}{\sin^4\theta}=\dfrac{4\tan^2\theta\cos^2\theta-4\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}{\sin^4\theta}=\dfrac{4\sin^2\theta-4\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}{\sin^4\theta}=\dfrac{4\sin^2\theta(1-\cos^2\theta)}{\sin^4\theta}=\dfrac{4\sin^4\theta}{\sin^4\theta}=4\). Hence \(m_1-m_2=2\). Proved.

Compare \(ay^2+bxy+ex+dy=0\) with \(Ax^2+2Hxy+By^2+2Gx+2Fy+C=0\): \(A=0,\ 2H=b\Rightarrow H=\tfrac{b}{2},\ B=a,\ 2G=e\Rightarrow G=\tfrac{e}{2},\ 2F=d\Rightarrow F=\tfrac{d}{2},\ C=0\). Condition for a pair of lines: \(ABC+2FGH-AF^2-BG^2-CH^2=0\). Substituting (\(A=0,C=0\)): \(2\cdot\tfrac{d}{2}\cdot\tfrac{e}{2}\cdot\tfrac{b}{2}-a\cdot\tfrac{e^2}{4}=0\Rightarrow \dfrac{bde}{4}-\dfrac{ae^2}{4}=0\Rightarrow bde=ae^2\), i.e. \(e(bd-ae)=0\). Hence the condition is \(bd=ae\) (for \(e\neq0\)).

If \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0\) (through origin) forms an equilateral triangle with a base line, the angle between the two lines is \(60^\circ\) and each makes \(60^\circ\) with the base. The tangent of the angle between the pair is \(\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3=\left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}\right|\Rightarrow 3(a+b)^2=4(h^2-ab)\Rightarrow 3a^2+6ab+3b^2=4h^2-4ab\Rightarrow 3a^2+10ab+3b^2=4h^2\). Factor the left side: \(3a^2+10ab+3b^2=(3a+b)(a+3b)\). Hence \((3a+b)(a+3b)=4h^2\). Proved.
diagramNote: Equilateral triangle: origin-pair and base line

solution: If \(x+2=0\) is one line of \(x^2+2xy+4y+k=0\), then substituting \(x=-2\) must make the equation an identity in \(y\) (the line lies on the locus). Put \(x=-2\): \((-2)^2+2(-2)y+4y+k=4-4y+4y+k=4+k\). For \(x=-2\) to be a factor, this must be \(0\) for all \(y\): \(4+k=0\Rightarrow k=-4\). Hence proved.

Let \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=b(y-m_1x)(y-m_2x)=0\), the lines \(y=m_1x,\ y=m_2x\) with \(m_1+m_2=-\tfrac{2h}{b},\ m_1m_2=\tfrac{a}{b}\). A line through the origin perpendicular to \(y=m_ix\) has slope \(-\tfrac{1}{m_i}\): \(x+m_iy=0\). The required pair is \((x+m_1y)(x+m_2y)=0\Rightarrow x^2+(m_1+m_2)xy+m_1m_2y^2=0\Rightarrow x^2-\tfrac{2h}{b}xy+\tfrac{a}{b}y^2=0\). Multiply by \(b\): \(bx^2-2hxy+ay^2=0\). Hence proved.

Write \(ax^2-y^2+2y+c-1=0\) (moving the \(1\)); \(A=a,\ B=-1,\ 2H=0\Rightarrow H=0,\ 2G=0\Rightarrow G=0,\ 2F=2\Rightarrow F=1,\ C=c-1\). For perpendicular lines the coefficient sum \(A+B=0\Rightarrow a-1=0\Rightarrow a=1\). For it to be a genuine pair of lines: \(ABC+2FGH-AF^2-BG^2-CH^2=0\Rightarrow (1)(-1)(c-1)+0-(1)(1)-0-0=0\Rightarrow -(c-1)-1=0\Rightarrow -c+1-1=0\Rightarrow c=0\). Hence \(a=1,\ c=0\).
